idiom_name: Alamofire RequestInterceptor/RetryPolicy + a UUID Idempotency-Key in the URLRequest
implementation_notes: URLSession has no documented automatic retry, so in practice the retry half comes from Alamofire: a RequestInterceptor (RequestAdapter plus RequestRetrier), its RetryPolicy, or a custom RequestRetrier that inspects the failed request and decides whether to replay it - and the documentation is explicit that a retry runs the complete pipeline again, adapters included. That is the trap: an adapter that stamps a fresh Idempotency-Key produces a new operation per attempt, so the key belongs at the call site (UUID().uuidString), stored with the pending work and attached to a URLRequest that the retrier replays unchanged. Use keyed requests for anything with side effects and reserve RetryPolicy for idempotent GETs and for keyed POSTs.
pitfalls: Alamofire re-runs the whole request pipeline for a retry, so a RequestAdapter that generates the key (or a fresh body) breaks the guarantee - the adapter must copy the persisted key, not invent one.
Retrying a request whose body cannot be replayed fails or duplicates; keep an in-memory body for keyed operations instead of a consumed stream.
Background URLSession tasks can be resumed by the system after the app restarts, so the key has to be persisted with the queued payload or the resubmission is a new operation.
